newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebed, Chechen leader to visit Council of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Lebed, Chechen leader to visit Council of Europe.

text.p: Russian security tsar Alexander Lebed and rebel Chechnya's chief of staff will discuss their peace deal before the Council of Europe parliamentary assembly on September 23, the 39-nation body said on Monday.

The Council said in a statement that Lebed and rebel chief of staff Aslan Maskhadov would attend the start of the assembly's September 23-27 session and would take part in a hearing on the situation in Chechnya.

Lebed, President Boris Yeltsin's national security adviser and secretary of his Security Council, signed a pact with the rebels on a peace mission last month. Russian troops began pulling out of Chechnya on Sunday under the deal, which is still in doubt.

The Council of Europe, which safeguards human rights and democracy, has condemned Russian military operations in Chechnya. Russia was allowed to join the Council in Feberuary, partly because it had pledged to avoid violence in settling the Chechen conflict.

The peace deal, signed after Moscow was humiliated by a rebel attack on Grozny, provides for the withdrawal of all Russian troops temporarily stationed in the region. But there is disagreement about what that involves.

The rebels say the fact that there were no troops in Chechnya before the conflict began in late 1994 means they must all pull out. The Russian side has said some troops will be based there permanently.
